title: How Paul Buchheit found his way to Google: keep moving, learn by joining startups
summary: Paul tells how he drifted into Silicon Valley with no plan, sent resumes to technically interesting startups, and ended up at Google despite doubting it would win. His lesson: you don't need it all figured out, so keep moving, seek uncertain opportunities, and treat early startup jobs as education.

principles.text: You don't need it all figured out; keep moving forward and seek uncertain, new opportunities.
principles.quote: You don't need to have it all figured out right now. The important thing is to keep moving forward. Seek opportunities to learn or try something new, something with uncertain outcomes.

principles.text: If you want startups, don't wait for the perfect one; join an interesting startup and learn.
principles.quote: If you're interested in startups, don't sit around waiting for the perfect opportunity, just go find one that sounds interesting and get a job there.

principles.text: Even a failing startup pays off because you learn far more than you otherwise would.
principles.quote: The startup will probably fail, but you will succeed because you have learned a lot more than you otherwise would have.

principles.text: The future is hard to predict; consensus about the 'wrong thing' is often wrong, as with Google in 1999.
principles.quote: In 1999 a lot of people thought that the world didn't need yet another search engine and that Google was the "wrong thing". The future is very difficult to predict.

principles.text: Join a business you truly believe in; otherwise pick a place where you can learn a lot.
principles.quote: If there is a business that you really believe in, then by all means join that. Otherwise, look at it more as a learning experience, a part of your education, and find someplace where you can learn a lot.

principles.text: Leave when life becomes too predictable and move toward something uncertain.
principles.quote: Last year I decided that life at Google had become too predictable, and too typical. I quit. It was time to move forward to something new, something uncertain.
